The summit of Camel’s Hump supports one of the Green Mountains’ three
significant communities of arctic-alpine vegetation. Many plants growing above
tree line are rare, threatened or endangered species in Vermont. These natural
communities are extremely fragile; the soils are very shallow and growing
conditions are very harsh. Hiker traffic through the area threatens the natural
community even more. Hikers should be aware that when a piece of alpine
tundra is destroyed, the wind rapidly scours holes in the damaged turf and the
soil erodes. Removal of rocks is equally detrimental. Travel only on marked
trails and rock outcrops. Keep pets on a leash and on the trail.
